column1: # What each pass of bin/refbias_run.sh consumes and produces.
# WHY A DECLARATION AND NOT A DERIVATION. Every pass already validates its own
# inputs -- each has a FATAL that names the file it could not find -- but that
# check happens inside the job, after the array has been submitted and after
# afterok has committed the rest of the chain to waiting on it. A missing input
# therefore costs a submission and cancels every downstream pass. This table
# moves the same knowledge in front of the submission, where it is cheap.
# It is also the answer to a second question: what does a pass READ? The
# per-cohort inventory records what each pass writes, which is half of an I/O
# contract, and a reader who wants to know whether a pass can run has had to
# scope   cohort  -- one file for the whole cohort
#         sample  -- one per isolate; `n` in the checker means the isolate count
#         build   -- a panel-wide asset, shared by every cohort
# when    pre     -- must exist before the pass is submitted
# required yes    -- the pass cannot run without it
#          no     -- optional; absence changes behaviour but is not an error
# exactly as bin/refbias_run.sh exports them, and ${S} for the sample.
